The value is a derived mix of two tokens in tokens.json (foreground 21.8%, muted_foreground 54.5%; 0.6*0.218+0.4*0.545 = 0.349 matches). The CSS holds a variable that derives from tokens, so there is no literal to replace. The derived shell variable is a deliberate nav-text step with no user-visible inconsistency.

The CSS defines .badge-primary{background:var(--tint-primary)} and light --tint-primary is color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-primary) 8%, var(--color-surface)), a tint built from the primary and surface tokens. Chrome serialises the mix as a srgb colour, which the checker cannot match to a token entry. The value is a derived tint of two tokens.

Dark badge background color(srgb 0.283469 0.0831975 0.115355) is the computed result of .badge-primary background var(--tint-primary), which the dark theme sets to color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-primary) 26%, var(--color-surface)); both inputs are tokens (primary, dark surface oklch(23.2% 0.02 272)). The dark overrides are documented in tokens.json meta.defaults_applied. The value is a derived tint, so there is no literal to replace. The contrast defect in this area is finding R-3, outside this verdict.
